newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina, Britain hold South Atlantic fish talks.
newsitem.headline: Argentina, Britain hold South Atlantic fish talks.

text.p: Argentina and Britain began a new round of talks Tuesday on fishing in the South Atlantic -- a major sticking point in otherwise fluid relations between the two former Falklands War enemies.

The Argentine Foreign Ministry said the 12th meeting of the bilateral South Atlantic Fishing Commission would last until Wednesday, and followed two days of talks in the seaside resort of Mar del Plata of a scientific sub-committee.
The talks in Buenos Aires are aimed at passing on to both governments "recommendations for the conservation of the most significant species in the area," the ministry said in a statement.
Britain and Argentina went to war in 1982 over the Falkland Islands, called the Malvinas in Argentina, but have restored diplomatic and trade links.
They have even come to an agreement about oil exploration in the British-run islands, which Argentina still claims as its own despite losing the 10-week war.

A long-term deal on protection of fish stocks, and especially of the ilex squid which are a major income source for the islanders, has proved elusive and squid catches have fallen rapidly in recent years.
